name: Dessert Shopping Cart
description: I took on the challenge to build a product list project that includes a functional cart.
imageAlt: Product page of desserts and a shopping cart.

details.description: This is my attempt at the Product List with Cart Frontend Challenge.

explination.heading: Project Purpose and Goal
explination.paragraph: I took on this challenge to continue to hone my skills. I wanted to test myself to see if I could utilize all of the techniques that I've gained thus far.

explination.heading: Web Stack and Explaination
explination.paragraph: I decided to use React.js so I can get more practice with it as well as Typescript. At this point, I am the most comfortable with Tailwind Css so I added it the this project. Here is the big challenge I made for myself, I added a backend to this project. I went with MERN stack since I learned it in school so I am somewhat familiar with it. I also added Cloudinary for managing the dessert images. I also deployed this project on Render.com, mainly because I sperated the frontend and the backend and I know that Render.com has options for a Static Site and also a Web Service for the backend.

explination.heading: Problems and Thought Process
explination.paragraph:
This was my first ever full stack project that I started from scratch. One of the issues that I came across was creating a function that would upload the image asset to Cloudinary, store the secure url in a varible that would then be uploaded to MongoDB where all the dessert data will be stored. I was able to solve this issue by using a async and await function to first upload the image to Cloudinary and then add the secure url to the dessert Mongoose Model to upload the data to MongoDB.

I can see that I still have room for improvement but, I am happy how this project turned out. Now to tackle user auth and login project.

name: Blackjack Web Game
description: Play a simple game of Blackjack. The one who is closest to 21 with out going over WINS!

details.description: Have a little fun play a simple game of Blackjack.

explination.heading: Project Purpose and Goal
explination.paragraph:
After taking the course of (CS 4220 - Current Trends in Web Design and Development), I wanted to test myself in seeing if I could build a Node.js/ Express.js project on my own.

My end goal was recreate the Blackjack game.

explination.heading: Web Stack and Explaination
explination.paragraph:
In class, we recreated the game of Poker so I used that as a guide. I used Node.js, Express.js for the application. I also use MongoDB for the database to store results of each game. Lastly, I used Axios for http requesting.

I also use the Deck of Card API to get card data.

explination.heading: Problems and Thought Process
explination.paragraph: One of the problems I came across was the feature to sum up the values of each card since the face card do not have a numerical value (according to the api), this issue is worse in the case if the Ace card. The way I was able to solve these issues was to essentially develop a function that accepts a card's value, if the card's value is not numerical change it to numerical.

imageAlt: Blackjack web app before start game is initiated.
